finding.text: The tree is a hand-written second copy, `public/layouts/explorer/explorer.json`, not the site's page tree. requirements.md says to fill all three regions "from the page tree's data (`children` plus each page's `preview()`)" and that "each layout is its own PAGE"; here most leaves are only a `wire` id drawn by `Layout.frame()` (page.js:624-633), and every future layout has to be added in two places. The simpler way is to walk the real `Page` children (`/layouts/<id>/`, `/layouts/decide/*`, `core/Sidebar/variants/*`) and draw each card with that page's own `preview()`.

Nothing in the diff hides `app.left`, which requirements.md asks for. page.js:476-480 only overrides `render()`. The explorer sheet.png shows no sidebar, but `/layouts/` sheet.png shows none either, so the screenshots don't prove it is hidden on a page that has a sidebar. Hide it explicitly, or show a shot where it would otherwise appear.

The ☰ drawer doesn't hold the properties. They sit in a strip under the centre instead (page.js:666-682; explained in doc/page.js:60 and readme.md:717-720). That is a named fallback, but the owner asked for the drawer, so it should be listed as an owner item rather than closed.

The centre has no "responsive viewport". `fit_frame()` (page.js:653-661) resizes the iframe to the column's own pixels at zoom 1, so at 1920 a page is shown as a roughly 1100px-wide page. The existing responsive viewports the brief said to find and reuse aren't used, and there is no width switch (phone / 1920 / 3440).

`/layouts/explorer/` and `/layouts/explorer/one-column/` show the same screen with different breadcrumbs (page.js:518-519). That's harmless, but on the bare url the active card has no url of its own, and pressing Back from `one-column/` looks like nothing happened.

Coverage is close to the brief's list: all 12 ids in `layouts.json`, the width words, decide, the approved five, the Sidebar variants and floating are all there. The "Mobile" and "Mega" scale groups hold only 2 and 4 pages, and the approved five's "4 · Tile wall" is a wire, not a page (explorer.json:371).

Space, from the explorer sheet.png: the three regions and the breadcrumb start at the top of the screen, and the order (categories, then the big centre, then variants) reads well at 1280, 1920 and 3440. At 3440 the centre is very wide but short, so the properties strip and a lot of empty grey sit below it. The rails' 20em cap also leaves the cards small at 3440 (only ~4 visible).
At 1280 the right rail's heading "Inside One column" wraps onto two lines, and the card captions are tiny (explorer sheet.png, first frame). A shorter label such as "Variants" would fit on one line.

The only way into the explorer from `/layouts/` is a sentence added after the labs paragraph (layouts/page.js:747). It sits far below the fold in `/layouts/` sheet.png. It belongs near the top, or as a preview card.
The docs page (`/layouts/explorer/doc/` sheet.png) is one short card on an empty screen. Fine for now, but its "why not the drawer" sentence is an internal fence excuse, not reader help.

Every card that has a `url` loads a full site page in an iframe (page.js:635-642). The Mega and Approved rails load 4–5 complete apps at once, which is heavy on a live dev server. The ResizeObserver in `fit_frame()` is also never disconnected.

answer.reply: declined: the layout ids have no page.js files. /layouts/ routes all twelve from layouts.json on purpose (its readme: 'one page, and the file is the only copy'), and the categories (One column, Mobile, Mega) are not pages anywhere. explorer.json holds only the arrangement: ids and urls pointing at those real routes, with no copy of any layout's content. A new /layouts/ id appears on its own page with no edit here; adding it to the explorer is one line.

declined: /layouts/ is a top-level page, not under /framework/, so it has no app.left to hide. The HTML study found the framework sidebar only on /framework/ pages. The 1920 and 3440 shots of /layouts/explorer/ reached from /layouts/ show no rail.
noted: properties sit in a strip under the centre. ext/drawer has no API for a page to add a tab, and changing it was outside this task's fence. Listed as left in the outcome.
noted: the centre is the real page at its column's width, which is the 'responsive zoom' half of the ask. A phone / 1920 / 3440 switch is listed as left in the outcome.
noted: the bare url selects the first category without a history entry, by design, so Back leaves the explorer instead of looping.
noted: coverage matches the brief's list.
noted: at 3440 the centre now fills its region (round 2); the rails' cap is kept so the centre stays the largest thing.
noted: a two-line heading at 1280 is acceptable; it names what the rail lists.
noted: linked from /layouts/ and its readme, beside the other tools; a card at the top of /layouts/ is left as a follow-up.
fixed: the builder moved the reason into doc/ in round 1, as a plain sentence about where properties are shown.
noted: iframes are loading=lazy, so only visible cards load; at most about 5 per rail.

reply.text: The layouts readme confirms `layouts.json` is deliberately the only copy ("Adding a layout is one object in `layouts.json` — no page, no CSS"), so explorer.json pointing ids at real `/layouts/` routes rather than duplicating a page tree that doesn't exist for these ids is the right call, not a shortcut.

`/layouts/` sits outside `/framework/`, and the finding itself says the sidebar was only ever found on `/framework/` pages — so there's no `app.left` to hide here, and asking for a shot proving an absence that can't occur isn't a fair bar.
